contributorNote: Borana / Oromo (Afaan Borana / Afaan Oromoo) dictionary compiled and verified line-by-line from Rev. J. L. Krapf & Rev. C. W. Isenberg ("Vocabulary of the Galla Language", London, CMS, 1842, pp. i–ii, 1–42 & "Vocabulary of Six East-African Languages", Tübingen, 1850 — Public Domain), Karl & Lawrence Tutschek ("Dictionary of the Galla Language, Part I: Galla–English–German [Munich, 1844, pp. i–lix, 1–205] & Part II: English–Galla [Munich, 1845, pp. 1–126]" & "A Grammar of the Galla Language", Munich, 1845, pp. i–viii, 1–92 — Public Domain), Wiktionary's Afroasiatic Swadesh list, and Wikipedia's Oromo language grammatical & lexical tables.

entries.translation: Nagaa / Naga, naga! Fayaketi! / Baga nagaan dhufte
entries.context: Borana / Oromo traditional greeting ('Peace, peace! Thy health!' — Tutschek 1845, p. 88, Aga's Letter)

entries.english: How are you? (Do you have peace?)
entries.translation: Nagaa qabdaa? / Akkam jirta? / Ati faya cabte?
entries.context: Borana / Oromo greeting & Tutschek (1845, p. 88)
Borana / Oromo response

entries.english: Good morning (Did you spend the night in peace?)
entries.translation: Bulte nagaa? / Akkam bulte? / Naga ambulte! (Krapf 1842)
entries.context: Borana / Oromo morning greeting (Krapf 1842, p. 16: "naga ambulte" = Good morning!; cf. bula "pass the night", Tutschek 1845)

entries.english: Good afternoon / Hast thou passed this day in peace?
entries.translation: Oolte nagaa? / Akkam oolte? / Ati naga olte har'a?
entries.pronunciation: ool-te na-gaa / a-ti na-ga ol-te har-a
entries.context: Tutschek (1845, p. 88, Aga's Letter: 'Ati naga olte had'a?')
Tutschek (1845, p. 90, closing of Otshu Aga's Letter)

entries.english: Rest in peace until we meet again
entries.translation: Nagan hafi hama nu wal agaruti
entries.pronunciation: na-gan ha-fi ha-ma nu wal a-ga-ru-ti
entries.context: Tutschek (1845, p. 91, closing of Akafed'e Dalle's Letter)

entries.english: Thank you / May God do good to him
entries.translation: Galatoomi (sg.) / Galatoomaa (pl.) / Wacayon iza ha tolu
entries.context: Borana / Oromo gratitude & Tutschek (1845, p. 90)
Borana / Oromo welcome

entries.translation: Nagaatti / Wak' nagaia si kakennu! (Farewell! May God give thee peace!) / Nagaia hafu tshedde
entries.context: Borana / Oromo farewell & Krapf (1842, pp. 13, 31: "wak' nagaia si kakennu", "nagaia hafu tshedde" = bid farewell, "feiuma tshedde / salamata tshedde" = greet)

entries.english: Yes (and answer to a call: O!)
entries.translation: Eeyyee / Ee (ee-djed'a = to say yes, affirm; o! = answer to a call)

entries.english: No / Not / It is not so
entries.context: Tutschek (1845, §§ 10, 175, p. 90: 'wau, akana miti')

entries.english: It shall be done! / Let it be so!
entries.context: Tutschek (1845, § 149, p. 44 — ready consent to a request)

entries.english: Come! / Come here! / Let us go!
entries.translation: Kod'u! (pl. Kod'a! / emph. Kod'uka!) / Benuka! (Benu / Bena!)

entries.context: Tutschek (1845, § 254, p. 82 — entreating particle mê)

entries.translation: inni, ini (he, acc. iza) / ishiin, iz'in (she, acc. ishii, iz'i)
maali? / mali? (mal, emph. maltu) / malif? (malifi, maf, mafi)

entries.english: How much? / How many? / Which of the two?
entries.translation: mêka? / kami? (emph. kamtu; izakamtu? = which of the two?)
